about.title: About Cerne Code
about.description: Local coding agent built with Rust (Tauri) and Vue.js. Thanks to all the creators of the open-source tools that make this project possible.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.text: Cerne Code performs real actions on your computer through artificial intelligence — files may be created, edited or deleted, and commands may be executed. Cerne Code is not responsible for actions performed by the AI. Use at your own risk.
disclaimer.subtext: In Manual mode (default), every action asks for your approval before running. Review each request carefully.

skillEditor.whatIsASkill: What a skill is: a SKILL.md file with instructions the agent loads on demand (via load_skill) when it notices they're relevant to the current request — a way to teach the agent a specific step-by-step process or convention without having to rewrite it every conversation.
skillEditor.whenToCreateOne: When it's worth creating one: when you catch yourself explaining the same thing to the agent across different conversations (a team process, a specific output format, the right steps to review a PR, etc.). The description is what the agent reads to decide whether the skill is relevant — make it clearly state WHEN to use it.
skillEditor.fillNameAndDescription: Fill in the name and "when to use it" before saving.

personaEditor.whatIsAPersona: Free text injected as a system instruction for this session when selected in the composer (e.g. "You are a senior Rust code reviewer, focused on security and performance"). Applies to the whole session, unlike a skill (which the agent loads on its own when it decides it's relevant).
personaEditor.whatIsAnAgent: An explicit step-by-step script the LLM follows as an orchestrator (e.g. "List the input folder, classify each file by type, then move it to the matching subfolder and confirm with the user before deleting the original"). Same mechanism as Persona underneath, but focused on ACTION (what to do, in what order) instead of tone/knowledge.

lfm3.title: LFM3 — LiquidAI models
lfm3.intro: Five small models that run on your machine through llama.cpp: text, vision, audio with speech, omni, and a decision classifier. They can work alone or alongside the chat to reduce what goes to the expensive model.

howTo.title: How to use
howTo.step1: Install llama.cpp b11960 or newer (the build must support LFM3).
howTo.step2: Enter the paths to llama-server.exe and models-lfm3.ini below and save the “lfm3” fork.
howTo.step3: Check that each model shows as “ready” on the cards.
howTo.step4: Use “Use in chat” for a chat model, or the tests below to try each function.

setup.title: Setup
setup.hint: Cerne does not assume where you installed anything: the paths are yours. models-lfm3.ini must have the sections lfm3-1.7b-text, lfm3-vl-2b, lfm3-audio-2b, lfm3-omni-2b and d1-omni-2b, each with model and mmproj (see the README in the LFM3 folder).
setup.label: Name

models.title: The 5 models
models.text: Text-only chat. The lightest: good for short answers and simple tasks.
models.vision: Chat with images. Describes photos, screenshots and scanned documents.
models.audio: Hears audio (transcription) and speaks the reply (TTS, via llama-tts). Language is chosen on this screen.
models.omni: Chat with image, audio and video, replying in text and voice. No internal reasoning.
models.decision: Not a chat model. Answers calibrated decision questions (yes/no, choice among options, score) without generating text.

when.text: Use for rewrites, short summaries and simple questions.
when.vision: Use when the conversation has an image and the chat model cannot see it.
when.audio: Use to dictate and hear replies with the same model.
when.omni: Use for voice conversation or for questions about a photo and audio together.
when.decision: Use before the chat for triage, routing and validation.

models.decisionNote: Use the classifier below or the /v1/systemone endpoint.

useCases.title: When to use it alongside the chat
useCases.intro: The idea is to send the expensive model only what it needs. Savings depend on your usage: measure with real prompts.

item1.title: Triage before the chat
item1.body: d1 classifies the message (topic, urgency, team) and only what needs a long answer goes to the chat model.

item2.title: Escalate only when needed
item2.body: A small model answers first; if d1's confidence is low, the question goes up to the large model.

item3.title: Audio becomes text first
item3.body: Transcribe locally with Audio or Omni and send only the text to the chat model, without sending audio to the cloud.

item4.title: Image becomes a short description
item4.body: VL describes the image in a few lines and that description goes to a text-only model.

item5.title: Local speech for replies
item5.body: Audio generates the spoken reply on your machine, with no paid TTS service.
